newsitem.title: USA: Texas Commerce, First Southwest to manage TexPool.
newsitem.headline: Texas Commerce, First Southwest to manage TexPool.

text.p: A team led by two Texas firms, Texas Commerce Bank and First Southwest Asset Management Inc of Dallas, will assume day-to-day administration of TexPool, the state's $6.2 billion investment fund, a state official said Friday.

"Under our contract with Texas Commerce/First Southwest, TexPool participants will be provided with an excellent level of service and at a significantly lower cost than in the past, without relinquishing the state's direction over how these funds are managed and invested," John Sharp, state comptroller of public accounts, stated in a release.
The investment pool is for cities, counties, school districts and other local government entities.

The Texas Commerce/First Southwest team will start immediately to transfer duties currently performed by the comptroller's Treasury Operations Division, formerly the State Treasury. The team is expected to assume complete management of TexPool in early May, the release said.

"Our job is to improve customer service for TexPool's 1,212 local participants," Sharp said. "We want to increase their investment earnings and provide a full range of asset, risk, and financial management services at a price and quality above the state's current performance."

Sharp said that after reviewing all the proposals, "our evaluation committee has determined that the Texas Commerce/First Southwest team can best manage TexPool's assets on behalf of participating local governments."

TexPool participants will save approximately $1.5 million annually in fees under management of the fund by Texas Commerce/First Southwest. The team will charge 5.5 basis points to administer the invested funds, according to the release.
